group.passage:
Every day in the United States, many people are killed in car crashes and nine percent of the deaths are caused by distracted driving. So, what is distracted driving and how distracted driving affects road users? Generally speaking, distracted driving means doing another activity which draws the driver’s attention away from operating his or her motor vehicles. This kind of activity can increase the chance of car crashes. Anything that may take a driver’s attention away from driving can be a distraction: sending a text message, talking on a mobile phone, using a navigation system, eating or drinking while driving, etc. Any of these distractions can endanger the driver, the passengers, and other people who are on the road.
There are three main types of distraction—visual, manual and cognitive. First, visual distraction refers to anything that will take your eyes off the road. Then, manual distraction means driving and taking your hands off the wheel, and last, cognitive distraction is that you take your mind off while driving.
In the United States in 2019, over 3,100 people were killed and about 424,000 were injured in crashes involving a distracted driver. About 1 in 5 of the people who died in crashes involving a distracted driver in 2019 were not in vehicles—they were walking, riding their bikes, or otherwise outside a vehicle. What’s surprising is that among fatal crashes involving distracted drivers, a higher percentage of drivers aged 15-20 were distracted than drivers aged 21 and older.
What can drivers, passengers, and parents do to avoid these crashes? First, do not multitask while driving. Whether it is adjusting your mirrors, selecting music, eating, making a phone call, or reading a text or email—do it before or after your trip, not during. Then, speak up if you are a passenger in a car with a distracted driver. Ask the driver to focus on his or her driving. A passenger can reduce distractions for the driver by assisting with navigation or other tasks. Last, parents are supposed to talk to your teen or young adult about the rules and responsibilities involved in driving. By sharing stories and statistics related to teen or young adult drivers and distracted driving, they will be more acquainted with the consequences of distracted driving.

figures.caption: 第1題選項 (A)–(D)：四張車內情境插圖
figures.description: 四張黑白車內情境插圖，各為一個選項。(A) 從後座看向車內前方：左座駕駛雙手握方向盤、注視前方道路上的兩輛車；右側副駕駛座的乘客低頭看著手中的手機。(B) 車窗外是街道與建築：畫面左側是車門外的側邊後照鏡（鏡中映出後方的建築與車輛），駕駛的一隻手伸到車門內側的後照鏡調整按鈕上調整後照鏡，另一隻手握著方向盤，人仍在開車。(C) 從車內後方看向前方擋風玻璃：後座一名乘客低頭看手中的手機，前座駕駛坐在座位上，車子行駛在道路上。(D) 一名女駕駛面帶微笑、雙手握方向盤注視前方；畫面右上方畫有一個大的「禁止使用手機」標誌（手機圖案加上圓形斜線禁止符號）。

figures.caption: 第2題選項 (A)–(D)：drivers’ age versus percentage of car crashes
figures.description: 四張水平長條圖，各為一個選項；縱軸由上而下為駕駛年齡層 15 - 20、21 - 24、25 - 34、35 - 44、45 - 54、55 - 64、65 - 74、75+，橫軸為百分比（刻度 0%、5%、10%），每條長條末端標示數值。各圖數值最高的長條以深灰色顯示：(A) 15 - 20；(B) 21 - 24；(C) 15 - 20 與 21 - 24；(D) 21 - 24。各圖數值見 rows。

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of distracted driving?

options.A: ［圖］從後座看向車內前方：駕駛（左座）雙手握方向盤、注視前方道路上的兩輛車；副駕駛座的乘客低頭看手中的手機。
options.B: ［圖］行車中，駕駛一手握方向盤，另一隻手伸到車門內側的後照鏡調整按鈕上調整左側後照鏡（後照鏡中映出後方的建築與車輛）。
options.C: ［圖］從車內後方看向前方：後座的乘客低頭看手中的手機，前座駕駛坐在座位上注視前方道路。
options.D: ［圖］女駕駛面帶微笑、雙手握方向盤注視前方；畫面旁有一個「禁止使用手機」標誌（手機圖案加上圓形斜線禁止符號）。

options.B: Thinking about what is bothering you while driving means that you are visually distracted.

options.D: Distracted driving affects all road users, including drivers, passengers, and others on the road.
